{{Short description|American author, poet, and wildlife biologist}}
'''Joseph Drew Lanham''' is an American author, poet, and wildlife biologist who was awarded a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Fellowship]] in 2022 for his work "combining conservation science with personal, historical, and cultural narratives of nature."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/features/drew-lanham-home-place-memoir/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180823085036/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/features/drew-lanham-home-place-memoir/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 23, 2018|title=Exploring Ties Between Nature, History, and Race|last=Long|first=Kat|date=2016-09-09|website=National Geographic|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.macfound.org/fellows/class-of-2022/joseph-drew-lanham#searchresults | title=Joseph Drew Lanham }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Raised in [[Edgefield, South Carolina]], Lanham studied zoology at [[Clemson University]], where he also earned a PhD in Forest Resources in 1997. He was named an Alumni Distinguished Professor at the university in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Endowed Chairs and Titled Professors |url=https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/research/about/endowed-chair.html |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=Endowed Chairs and Titled Professors |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/faculty_staff/profiles/lanhamj|title=Employee Profiles {{!}} College of Agriculture, Forestry and Life Sciences {{!}} Clemson University, South Carolina|website=www.clemson.edu|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref> He currently teaches several classes on birding and wildlife science. He describes his work in his own words as: "’Connecting the conservation dots’ is how I envision my research mission. My past work has focused on the impacts of forest management and other human activities on songbirds, herpetofauna, small mammals and butterflies. More recently I've begun to investigate how ethnicity (especially Black Americans) relate to wildlife and other conservation issues. I'm also interested in how birders and hunters might bridge philosophical gaps to effect conservation in a more holistic way."

His research focuses on songbird ecology. He is a board member of several conservation organizations, including the South Carolina Wildlife Federation, Audubon South Carolina, the [[Aldo Leopold Foundation]], [[BirdNote]], and the [[American Birding Association]], and an advisory board member for the North American Association of Environmental Education.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.audubon.org/content/dr-j-drew-lanham|title=Dr. J. Drew Lanham|date=2017-10-27|website=Audubon|language=en|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref> In 2016, he was named a Brandwein Fellow for his work in environmental education, and he has also been a fellow of Toyota TogetherGreen and the Clemson University Institute for Parks. Lanham is a Board member of the [[National Audubon Society]]; in 2019 he was awarded its Dan W. Lufkin Prize for Environmental Leadership, recognizing "individuals who have dedicated their entire lives to the environment".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.audubon.org/dan-w-lufkin-prize-environmental-leadership|title=Dan W. Lufkin Prize for Environmental Leadership|date=2015-01-09|website=Audubon|language=en|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://newsstand.clemson.edu/mediarelations/clemson-professor-j-drew-lanham-to-be-honored-by-national-audubon-society/|title=Clemson professor J. Drew Lanham to be honored by National Audubon Society|website=Newsstand {{!}} Clemson University News and Stories, South Carolina|date=18 December 2018|access-date=2019-04-23|archive-date=2019-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423052626/http://newsstand.clemson.edu/mediarelations/clemson-professor-j-drew-lanham-to-be-honored-by-national-audubon-society/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his 20 years as a faculty member, he has taught courses, conducted research and outreach in woodland ecology, conservation biology, forest biodiversity, wildlife policy and conservation ornithology and has mentored more than 40 students.

Lanham is a strong advocate for the African American role in natural resources conservation, intrigued with how culture and ethnic prisms can bend perceptions of nature and its care. Lanham believes that conservation must be a blending of head and heart, rigorous science and evocative art. In 2013, Lanham wrote a piece for ''[[Orion (online magazine)|Orion Magazine]]'' titled "9 Rules for the Black Birdwatcher,"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://orionmagazine.org/article/9-rules-for-the-black-birdwatcher/|title=9 Rules for the Black Birdwatcher|last=Lanham|first=J. Drew|date=December 2013|website=Orion Magazine|language=en|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/grrlscientist/2015/mar/04/rules-for-the-black-birdwatcher|title=Rules for the black birdwatcher|date=2015-03-04|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-04-23|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> drawing attention to the lack of Black birders and diversity in general among naturalists. The short piece inspired producer Ari Daniel and videographer Amanda Kowalski to create a short film with the same title for ''[[BirdNote]],''<ref>{{Citation|last=BirdNote|title=Rules for the Black Birdwatcher - With Drew Lanham|date=2015-02-28|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4thb2zGuOnU|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=Bird-Watching While Black: A Wildlife Ecologist Shares His Tips|url=https://video.nationalgeographic.com/video/short-film-showcase/00000156-b92d-dbd5-add6-bbef15820000|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423025848/https://video.nationalgeographic.com/video/short-film-showcase/00000156-b92d-dbd5-add6-bbef15820000|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 23, 2019|work=National Geographic|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref> which quickly went viral on social media.<ref name=":0" /> In 2016 he wrote "Birding While Black."<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-09-22|title=Birding While Black|url=https://lithub.com/birding-while-black/|access-date=2020-06-03|website=Literary Hub|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2017 he published the award-winning memoir ''The Home Place: Memoirs of a Colored Man's Love Affair with Nature''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The home place : memoirs of a colored man's love affair with nature|last=Lanham, J. Drew (Joseph Drew)|isbn=978-1571313508|edition= First paperback |location=Minneapolis, Minnesota|oclc=959536553|date = 2017-06-13}}</ref> His book received the Reed Award from the [[Southern Environmental Law Center]] and the Southern Book Prize, and was a finalist for the [[John Burroughs Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-07-21 |title=J. Drew Lanham |url=https://milkweed.org/author/j-drew-lanham |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=Milkweed Editions |language=en}}</ref> The book was listed in ''[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]'' as one of the 11 best scholarly books of the 2010s, chosen by [[Anna Tsing]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-04-14|title=The Best Scholarly Books of the Decade|url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/the-best-scholarly-books-of-the-decade/|access-date=2020-12-26|website=The Chronicle of Higher Education}}</ref> Lanham features in episode 7 of the 2019 TV series ''[[Birds of North America (TV series)|Birds of North America]]'', produced by Topic and hosted by [[Jason Ward (naturalist)|Jason Ward]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.topic.com/birds-of-north-america/drew-lanham-hope-is-the-thing-with-feathers|title=Drew Lanham: Hope Is the Thing With Feathers|website=Topic|language=en|access-date=2019-04-23|archive-date=2019-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423054228/https://www.topic.com/birds-of-north-america/drew-lanham-hope-is-the-thing-with-feathers|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/4/3/18291212/birding-youtube-nature-show-documentary-topic-animals-jason-ward|title=Birding gets new life in this YouTube nature series|last=Becker|first=Rachel|date=2019-04-03|website=The Verge|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref> In 2020, the podcast ''[[This Is Love (podcast)|This Is Love]]'' spoke with Lanham for their episode, "Prairie Warbler."<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 13, 2020|title=Prairie Warbler|url=https://thisislovepodcast.com/episode-22-prairie-warbler|website=[[This Is Love (podcast)|This is Love]]}}</ref> In December 2020, he received the E. O. Wilson Biodiversity Award for Outstanding Science, Advocacy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://biologicaldiversity.org/w/news/press-releases/clemson-ornithologist-named-2020-eo-wilson-biodiversity-award-recipient-2020-12-16/|title = Clemson Ornithologist Named 2020 E.O. Wilson Biodiversity Award Recipient}}</ref> In 2021, Lanham wrote an essay for the Autumn 2021 issue of Living Bird, entitled "Wildness on A Whim: Reflections On Whimbrel In The South Carolina Lowcountry."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-13 |title=Wildness on a Whim: Reflections on Whimbrel in the South Carolina Lowcountry |url=https://www.allaboutbirds.org/news/wildness-on-a-whim-reflections-on-whimbrel-in-the-south-carolina-lowcountry/ |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=All About Birds |language=en-US}}</ref> Lanham was recognized in February 2022 by the ''Post and Courier'' newspaper (Charleston, SC) as one of twelve Black Leaders in South Carolina.

== Personal life ==
Lanham is married to Janice Garrison Lanham, a senior lecturer in the School of Nursing at Clemson University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty Scholars {{!}} Clemson University, South Carolina |url=https://www.clemson.edu/health-research/faculty/lanham.html |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=www.clemson.edu}}</ref> They have two adult children. He and his family live in the Upstate of South Carolina.
